Exclude moderator/bot notices. Return 1 if at least one comment explicitly quotes (quote markup or verbatim OP wording) or explicitly references a specific identifiable textual element of the OP's title or argument (a particular sentence, phrase, claim or example the OP wrote), whether or not it agrees with, endorses or refutes it. Exclude from OP context any OP view-change/delta-award announcements, post-outcome thank-you/resolution updates, and any text reporting whether the outcome occurred; do not use such text to establish a match. Generic discussion of delta/platform rules is allowed. Use current supplied text; do not infer an initial snapshot or chronology from list order. Return 0 if the comment list is validly empty or no comment qualifies given available OP text. Return null if OC_comments is missing or malformed, or if both OP title and argument are missing so absence cannot be determined (an observed match to available OP text may still be 1).

features.name: oc_comments_lexical_density
features.definition: OC_comments (other users' counter-argument comments): pooled lexical density, i.e., content words as a share of all words across all comments in the row.
features.spec: Parse OC_comments as a JSON list of strings (other users' comments, not the OP; OP view-change/delta-award announcements, thank-you/resolution updates and outcome-reporting text by the OP are not part of this field and no other column is read). If missing or unparseable, return null. If the list is empty, or contains zero word tokens in total, return null. Otherwise lowercase each comment, tokenize words with re.findall(r"[a-z']+", text) (drop tokens with no letters), and pool tokens across all comments. A token is a function word if it is in the NLTK English stopword list (nltk.corpus.stopwords.words('english')); all other tokens are content words. Return content_word_count / total_word_count (range 0-1; higher means denser). Comments are pooled by tokens (longer comments weigh more); this pooling is an operational assumption, not from the hypothesis.

Exclude and ignore any OP view-change or delta-award announcements, post-outcome thank-you or resolution updates, and any text reporting whether the outcome occurred, even if they express thanks or support; generic discussion of delta/platform rules is not an outcome announcement and is not itself a request. Return null if argument is missing or malformed. Output a single 0/1 value.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Discussions where the original argument includes explicit comparisons to established scientific or historical norms are associated with lower view change than those without such comparisons.
hypotheses.h0: Rows with arg_compares_to_scientific_or_historical_norms=1 have the same delta rate as rows with 0.
hypotheses.h1: Rows with arg_compares_to_scientific_or_historical_norms=1 have lower delta rate than rows with 0.
hypotheses.note: Measures current argument text, which may include edits; the initial snapshot is not reconstructed. Association only, not causal. "Established" norms is judged semantically by the annotator, no external verification.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Arguments expressing explicit fear of social rejection or isolation are associated with lower view-change rates than arguments stating beliefs without emotional self-defense.
hypotheses.h0: There is no difference in delta rate between rows with op_expresses_fear_of_social_rejection_or_isolation and rows with op_states_beliefs_without_emotional_self_defense.
hypotheses.h1: Rows with op_expresses_fear_of_social_rejection_or_isolation have a lower delta rate than rows with op_states_beliefs_without_emotional_self_defense.
hypotheses.note: The claim is a contrast between fear-of-rejection rows and no-self-defense rows. In the joint model each coefficient is relative to a residual group (other emotional self-defense without that fear), so no single coefficient equals the claimed contrast (it is beta_fear minus beta_nodefense). Hence term=null. Measures use current OP text (title and argument), not an initial snapshot. Edits are not removed and outcome announcements are excluded by the annotator. Associations only.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Counter-arguments that cite specific, functioning institutional precedents are associated with a higher probability of view change than those relying on abstract normative principles.
hypotheses.h0: The coefficient on any_comment_cites_functioning_institutional_precedent minus that on any_comment_relies_on_abstract_normative_principles is zero (equal association with delta).
hypotheses.h1: Precedent-citing comments are associated with higher delta probability than abstract-normative comments (difference > 0).
hypotheses.note: With T = precedent + normative, y = a*P + b*N = (a-b)*P + b*T, so the P coefficient is beta_precedent - beta_normative, the claimed contrast. Features are any-comment indicators, not exclusive groups; rows can have both or neither. Comment order and timing are unavailable; associations only, not causal. Comparison group is abstract-normative reliance, not not-precedent.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Discussions featuring longer precomputed log-transformed discussion length are associated with a higher likelihood of the original poster changing their view.
hypotheses.h0: supplied_log_length has no association with the likelihood of delta (coefficient = 0).
hypotheses.h1: Higher supplied_log_length is associated with a higher likelihood of delta (coefficient > 0).
hypotheses.note: log_length construction, source text, log base and timing relative to the outcome are undocumented; it may include post-outcome text, and it is not equated with argument word count. Association only, not causal.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Discussions where the original argument contains explicit admissions of uncertainty are associated with a higher probability of view change than those asserting absolute certainty.
hypotheses.h0: Discussions whose OP argument has explicit uncertainty admissions (op_argument_admits_uncertainty) have no higher probability of view change than those asserting absolute certainty (op_argument_asserts_absolute_certainty).
hypotheses.h1: Discussions with op_argument_admits_uncertainty have a higher probability of view change than those with op_argument_asserts_absolute_certainty.
hypotheses.note: The claim compares uncertainty-admitting arguments with absolutely-certain ones, i.e. beta_uncertainty minus beta_certainty. No single OLS coefficient represents that contrast, because each coefficient is relative to the neither-group baseline. The two features are not complements, and the neither group is not the comparison group, so term=null. The features use current argument text with outcome-announcement text excluded. Marked edits cannot be timed, and no initial snapshot is reconstructed. Associations only.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Counter-arguments frequently challenging multiple distinct factual premises within the argument are positively associated with view change.
hypotheses.h0: multiple_factual_premises_challenged has no association with delta.
hypotheses.h1: Rows where comments challenge multiple distinct factual premises (multiple_factual_premises_challenged=1) have higher delta rates.
hypotheses.note: The hypothesis says "frequently" without a frequency cutoff; "multiple" is operationalized as >=2 distinct challenged factual premises across the row's comments (an assumption, not a tuned cutoff). The count is retained as the base measurement. The comment list is unordered and has no timing, so no pre-outcome exposure claim; current text is used with outcome announcements excluded. Association only, not causal.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Discussions where the original argument contains fewer counter-argument responses are associated with a lower likelihood of the original poster changing their view.
hypotheses.h0: oc_comment_count has no association with the likelihood of the OP changing their view.
hypotheses.h1: Higher oc_comment_count (more counter-argument comments) is associated with a higher likelihood of the OP changing their view, i.e., fewer comments with lower likelihood.
hypotheses.note: Hypothesis wording "original argument contains fewer counter-argument responses" is interpreted as the number of available other-user counter-argument comments in OC_comments for the discussion. Counts reflect supplied available comments only (observed range 1-17, none empty), which may be a sample; not distinct commenters; list order and timing unknown. Association only, not causal. No fixed threshold for "fewer" is specified, so a linear count is used.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Discussions with at least three distinct counter-arguments in the posted comments are associated with a higher likelihood of the original poster changing their view.
hypotheses.h0: at_least_three_distinct_counterarguments has no association with the likelihood of delta.
hypotheses.h1: Rows with at_least_three_distinct_counterarguments=1 have higher likelihood of delta than rows with 0.
hypotheses.note: Associational only. Counts use supplied current comments (available counter-argument comments, which may be a subset); distinctness is a semantic judgment. The count feature is the base measurement; the threshold of 3 comes from the hypothesis. Comment timing is unavailable and OLS on binary delta is a linear probability model.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Discussions where the original post title uses absolute certainty markers are associated with a lower likelihood of the original poster changing their view.
hypotheses.h0: Title absolute certainty markers (title_uses_absolute_certainty_markers) are not associated with the likelihood of delta.
hypotheses.h1: Discussions with title_uses_absolute_certainty_markers = 1 have a lower likelihood of delta than those with 0.
hypotheses.note: Association only, not causal. Uses current supplied title text; no time restriction claimed. Absolute certainty is judged semantically with no frequency or cutoff beyond presence of any marker.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Discussions where original posts explicitly invite critique or use tentative language are associated with higher view-change rates than those using absolute, definitive declarations.
hypotheses.h0: View-change rates do not differ between discussions with `op_invites_critique_or_tentative` and those with `op_absolute_definitive_declaration`.
hypotheses.h1: Discussions with `op_invites_critique_or_tentative` have higher view-change rates than those with `op_absolute_definitive_declaration`.
hypotheses.note: The claim compares invite/tentative posts against absolute/definitive posts (beta_A - beta_B). In this OLS each coefficient is relative to the omitted group (neither feature), so no single coefficient represents the contrast; term=null. The two features are not complements and may overlap. Measures use current supplied text, with outcome announcements excluded semantically; no initial snapshot is reconstructed. Associations only.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Discussions featuring counter-arguments that explicitly cite specific real-world examples are associated with higher likelihood of original view change.
hypotheses.h0: any_comment_cites_specific_real_world_example has no association with the likelihood of delta (view change).
hypotheses.h1: Rows with any_comment_cites_specific_real_world_example = 1 are associated with a higher likelihood of delta.
hypotheses.note: Association only. The hypothesis says "counter-arguments that explicitly cite examples" without a frequency rule, so the any-comment measure is used. OC_comments is unordered and has no timestamps, so exposure timing is not established. Current text is used, with outcome announcements excluded.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Counterarguments containing measured, logical reasoning are positively associated with the original poster changing their mind compared to those containing emotional aggression in ChangeMyView discussions.
hypotheses.h0: The coefficient on logical_minus_aggression_share is zero, i.e. the association of share_comments_measured_logical with delta equals that of share_comments_emotional_aggression.
hypotheses.h1: The association of share_comments_measured_logical with delta is more positive than that of share_comments_emotional_aggression (positive coefficient on logical_minus_aggression_share).
hypotheses.note: Reparametrization: with D=A-B and S=A+B, the coefficient on D equals (bA-bB)/2, the contrast between the logical (A) and aggressive (B) shares; S is only the algebraic complement, not an added control. Comments are treated as non-exclusive categories (a comment can be neither or in principle both); row share is the assumed aggregation, since the hypothesis does not specify any/share or a frequency cutoff. Rows with empty comment lists get null shares. Associations only, not causal. Current text used; no pre-outcome snapshot is claimed and comment order/timing is unavailable.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Discussions where counter-arguments explicitly quote and refute specific factual claims in the original post are associated with higher rates of view change.
hypotheses.h0: any_comment_quotes_and_refutes_op_factual_claim has no association with delta (view change).
hypotheses.h1: Rows with any_comment_quotes_and_refutes_op_factual_claim=1 are associated with higher view-change rates than rows with 0.
hypotheses.note: Association only, not causal. "Discussions where counter-arguments..." is operationalized as any comment (not a share or frequency; no cutoff specified). Comment order/timing unavailable; current text used with outcome-announcement exclusion. Quote must be of OP title/argument; conversation not used.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Discussions where counter-arguments explicitly validate the original poster's personal dignity or effort before introducing corrective logic are associated with higher view-change rates than purely logical refutations.
hypotheses.h0: any_comment_validates_op_dignity_or_effort_before_correction has no association with view-change (delta) rate.
hypotheses.h1: Rows with any_comment_validates_op_dignity_or_effort_before_correction = 1 have a higher view-change rate than rows with 0.
hypotheses.note: Comparison group is rows with no qualifying validating comment, which includes purely logical refutations but also other non-validating styles; the hypothesis's "purely logical" group is not separately isolated (it would require a semantic judgment of all comments as purely logical, not added to avoid inventing a control). Association only, not causal. Comment order within the list is unknown, but "before" is assessed within a single comment's text. Current supplied text is used; no timing snapshot is inferred.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Discussions featuring counter-arguments that provide concrete real-world examples are associated with a higher likelihood of view change than those relying primarily on abstract reasoning.
hypotheses.h0: any_comment_cites_specific_real_world_example has no association with delta, holding comments_primarily_abstract_reasoning fixed.
hypotheses.h1: Rows with any_comment_cites_specific_real_world_example=1 have higher likelihood of delta than rows without, holding comments_primarily_abstract_reasoning fixed.
hypotheses.note: Association only. The claim contrasts concrete-example discussions with primarily-abstract ones; the two features overlap and are not complements, so the single coefficient only approximates the contrast. 'Primarily' has no specified cutoff; holistic majority is an annotation assumption. Comment order and timing unavailable; current text used. Rows with empty comment lists would be null on the abstract feature (all rows here have at least one comment).

hypotheses.hypothesis: Discussions where counter-arguments explicitly engage with the specific examples or premises cited in the original argument text are associated with a higher likelihood of view change.
hypotheses.h0: any_comment_engages_op_cited_examples_or_premises has no association with delta.
hypotheses.h1: Rows where any_comment_engages_op_cited_examples_or_premises is 1 have a higher likelihood of delta=1.
hypotheses.note: Hypothesis says "counter-arguments ... engage" without a frequency cutoff; operationalized as any comment (assumption). Measured on current text; comment timing is unavailable, and associations are not causal. OC_comments order is not chronology.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Discussions featuring counter-arguments that introduce concrete, personal labor-process details are associated with higher view-change rates than those relying solely on abstract normative principles.
hypotheses.h0: Rows where any comment has concrete personal labor-process details (any_comment_concrete_personal_labor_details) have no different delta rate than rows where all comments rely solely on abstract normative principles (any_comment_relies_on_abstract_normative_principles).
hypotheses.h1: Rows with any_comment_concrete_personal_labor_details have higher delta rate than rows with any_comment_relies_on_abstract_normative_principles.
hypotheses.note: The claim is a contrast between two named groups (labor-detail vs solely-abstract). In the joint model each coefficient is relative to rows with neither property, so no single coefficient equals the contrast (it needs beta_A - beta_B); term=null. The features are mutually exclusive by definition. Rows with no comments are null for the solely-abstract feature. Measurements use current text; no temporal snapshot is available. Association only.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Discussions where counter-arguments explicitly quantify systemic material harms to third parties rather than asserting propositional falsity are associated with a higher likelihood of view change.
hypotheses.h0: any_comment_quantifies_systemic_third_party_harm has no association with delta, holding any_comment_asserts_propositional_falsity constant.
hypotheses.h1: Rows where any_comment_quantifies_systemic_third_party_harm is 1 have higher likelihood of view change, holding any_comment_asserts_propositional_falsity constant.
hypotheses.note: Association only. The claim's "rather than" contrast is approximated by two non-exclusive binary features with the harm coefficient adjusted for falsity assertion; it is not a strict harm-only vs falsity-only comparison. "Any comment" aggregation and the notion of "systemic" are operational assumptions; no frequency cutoff specified. Comments are unordered with no timing.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Discussions where counter-arguments identify logical contradictions within the original post's own stated premises are associated with higher view-change rates than those citing external evidence.
hypotheses.h0: Discussion-level view-change rates (delta) do not differ between discussions with any_comment_identifies_op_internal_contradiction and discussions with any_comment_cites_external_evidence.
hypotheses.h1: Discussions with any_comment_identifies_op_internal_contradiction have higher delta rates than those with any_comment_cites_external_evidence.
hypotheses.note: Claim is a contrast (beta_contradiction - beta_external) between named groups; no single OLS coefficient in this model represents it, and the two features can overlap, so term=null rather than testing one coefficient. Features use current supplied text; comment order/timing unavailable. Associations only.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Discussions where counter-arguments provide specific factual data or verifiable citations are associated with a higher likelihood of the original poster changing their view.
hypotheses.h0: any_comment_specific_factual_data_or_citation has no association with delta.
hypotheses.h1: Rows where any_comment_specific_factual_data_or_citation is 1 are associated with a higher likelihood of delta.
hypotheses.note: "Discussions where counter-arguments provide" is operationalized as any comment (not share/count; no frequency cutoff specified). Measures current supplied comment text; verifiability is judged from the text only, with no external checking. Association only, not causal.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Discussions where the original argument contains explicit polite apology phrases are associated with a lower likelihood of view change compared to arguments without such phrases.
hypotheses.h0: op_argument_has_polite_apology is not associated with the likelihood of view change (delta).
hypotheses.h1: Arguments with op_argument_has_polite_apology = 1 are associated with a lower likelihood of view change than those with 0.
hypotheses.note: Measured on current supplied argument text, not an initial snapshot (edit timing unknown); outcome announcements are excluded by instruction. 'Explicit polite apology phrase' has no fixed lexicon; the examples are nonexhaustive. Association only, not causal.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Original posts featuring first-person vulnerable admissions are associated with higher view-change likelihood than those containing distant, third-person observations.
hypotheses.h0: Rows with op_first_person_vulnerable_admission are not associated with higher delta likelihood than rows with op_distant_third_person_observation.
hypotheses.h1: op_first_person_vulnerable_admission is associated with higher delta likelihood than op_distant_third_person_observation.
hypotheses.note: The claim compares two named groups (A vs B), i.e. beta_A - beta_B, not a single coefficient; in an OLS with both indicators beta_A alone is A holding B fixed and does not represent the contrast, and the groups can overlap, so term=null. Measures use current OP text (edits retained, outcome announcements excluded); no initial snapshot is reconstructed. Semantic judgments are operational labels with no frequency cutoff.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Discussions where counter-arguments include direct URLs or external links are associated with a higher likelihood of view change than those solely using internal text.
hypotheses.h0: any_comment_contains_url has no association with the likelihood of view change.
hypotheses.h1: Rows with any_comment_contains_url = 1 have a higher likelihood of view change than rows with 0 (counter-arguments only using internal text).
hypotheses.note: Association only. Link detection is literal (http(s):// or www.); bare domains without scheme or www are not detected. The comparison group is rows with no detected link in any comment ("solely internal text"); rows mixing links and text count as 1. Comment timing/order is unavailable. The binary any-link feature is used since the claim does not specify a count or share.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Discussions where counter-arguments employ specific, verifiable procedural examples are associated with higher original post view-change rates than those relying solely on abstract theoretical rebuttals.
hypotheses.h0: Rows with any_comment_specific_verifiable_procedural_example have the same delta rate as rows with all_comments_solely_abstract_theoretical_rebuttal.
hypotheses.h1: Rows with any_comment_specific_verifiable_procedural_example have a higher delta rate than rows with all_comments_solely_abstract_theoretical_rebuttal.
hypotheses.note: The claim contrasts procedural-example rows with solely-abstract rows. Both are modeled, but the contrast (beta_procedural - beta_abstract) is not a single design-matrix coefficient, and each coefficient is relative to a residual baseline, so term=null. The second feature is null for empty lists, though lists are nonempty in the data. Associations only; operationalization of 'verifiable' uses supplied text without external checking.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Discussions where the original argument contains specific counter-question markers are associated with a higher probability of view change.
hypotheses.h0: op_argument_has_counter_question is not associated with delta probability.
hypotheses.h1: op_argument_has_counter_question is associated with a higher probability of view change (delta).
hypotheses.note: "Specific counter-question markers" is not defined in the hypothesis; operationalized as explicit questions posing a challenge to opposing views or inviting rebuttal, which is an interpretation. Uses current argument text including marked edits; no initial snapshot is reconstructed, and outcome announcements are excluded by instruction. Association only, not causal.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Discussions where the original poster's argument includes personal anecdotes or first-person experiential narratives are associated with a lower likelihood of view change.
hypotheses.h0: op_argument_has_personal_anecdote has no association with delta (view change).

hypotheses.note: Measures current supplied argument text, which may include marked edits; no initial snapshot is reconstructed. Outcome-reporting text is excluded via the prompt, which is a semantic exclusion. Association only, not causal.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Discussions where counter-arguments explicitly acknowledge the validity of the original post's initial premise before introducing divergence are associated with a higher likelihood of view change.
hypotheses.h0: any_comment_acknowledges_op_premise_before_diverging is unrelated to the likelihood of view change.
hypotheses.h1: Rows with any_comment_acknowledges_op_premise_before_diverging = 1 have a higher likelihood of view change.
hypotheses.note: Association only. The hypothesis says "counter-arguments" without specifying any/all/frequency; "any comment" is an operational assumption. "Initial premise" is interpreted as the OP's premise/main claim in the supplied current title/argument; no initial snapshot is reconstructable (edits may exist, timing unknown). Comment order and timing unavailable.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Discussions where counter-arguments employ concrete personal anecdotes are more likely associated with the original poster changing their view than those using abstract reasoning.
hypotheses.h0: Association of delta with any_comment_concrete_personal_anecdote is not greater than with comments_primarily_abstract_reasoning.
hypotheses.h1: Discussions with any_comment_concrete_personal_anecdote have higher delta likelihood than those with comments_primarily_abstract_reasoning.
hypotheses.note: The claim is a contrast (anecdote vs abstract) which equals beta_anecdote - beta_abstract; no single design-matrix coefficient represents it, so term=null. The two features can overlap (a row may have both), so they are not mutually exclusive groups. Measures current supplied comment text; no comment chronology is available. Associations only.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Discussions containing at least three distinct counter-argument comments are associated with a higher probability of the original poster changing their view than those with fewer.
hypotheses.h0: has_at_least_three_oc_comments has no association with the probability of delta (OP view change).

hypotheses.note: "Distinct" is operationalized as distinct list entries; the list may contain multiple comments from the same commenter and distinct commenters cannot be identified. OC_comments lists only available counter-argument comments, which may not be all comments in the discussion. Association only, not causal. Observed list length ranges 1-17 (no empty lists in the corpus).

hypotheses.hypothesis: Posts containing direct counterarguments are more likely to result in the original poster upvoting the reply or changing their view.

hypotheses.h1: Rows with any_comment_direct_counterargument = 1 have a higher likelihood of delta = 1.
hypotheses.note: Delta is the fixed outcome: it covers the OP changing their view (and delta award), but "upvoting the reply" is not separately measured. Association only, not causal. Comments are current text with no chronology; the unordered list gives no timing. Comparison is with rows lacking direct counterarguments, which may be rare since the dataset consists of counter-argument comments.

Exclude moderator/bot notices. Exclude any OP view-change or delta-award announcements, post-outcome thank-you/resolution updates and any text reporting whether the outcome occurred; generic discussion of delta/platform rules is not an outcome announcement and remains eligible. Use supplied current text; list order is not chronology or rank. Empty list returns null; missing or malformed input returns null. Output a single number 0-10.

right_feature.spec: Read OC_comments (JSON list of counter-argument comments by users other than the OP; parse it). Return 1 if at least one comment explicitly references a specific, concrete example or real-world instance (an actual named or particular case, event, person, organization, study result, or concrete personal experience) as part of its argument. Endorsement or verification is not required; the example need not be institutional or public. Invented/hypothetical scenarios and purely abstract generalizations do not count. Ignore any text that is an OP view-change/delta-award announcement, post-outcome thank-you/resolution update, or text reporting whether the outcome occurred; generic discussion of delta/platform rules is neither such an announcement nor an example. Return 0 if the list is valid and no comment qualifies, including when it is empty. Return null if OC_comments is missing or malformed. List order carries no meaning. Use only current supplied text; no initial snapshot is inferred.

right_feature.spec: Read OC_comments (JSON list of comments by users other than the OP; parse it) together with the OP's title and argument as context for what counts as OP wording. For each comment decide whether it contains a direct quotation of wording from the OP's title or argument (verbatim or near-verbatim text, typically in quotation marks or block-quote markup, that matches available OP text). Endorsement, refutation or agreement is not required. Paraphrases without quoted wording do not count; quoting other commenters or external sources does not count. Ignore and do not count quotations of OP view-change/delta-award announcements, post-outcome thank-you/resolution updates or any text reporting whether the outcome occurred (even if in argument); generic discussion of delta/platform rules remains eligible text. Use current supplied text; do not infer timing. Output the number of comments with a qualifying quote divided by the total number of comments in the list (range 0 to 1; 0 if none quote). If OC_comments is an empty list return null; if OC_comments, title or argument is missing/malformed such that quote matching cannot be determined return null (a positive match with available OP text may still be returned as such only if the comment share can be computed).

Return 0 if no such absolute/definitive declaration of the OP's view appears. Ignore quotations of others not adopted by the OP and standard CMV boilerplate/moderator notices. Do not reconstruct an initial snapshot. Return null if both title and argument are missing or malformed.

right_feature.name: counterargument_cognitive_complexity
right_feature.definition: Other-user counterargument comments: overall cognitive complexity (0-10) of the reasoning, i.e. differentiating multiple perspectives/considerations, acknowledging nuance or conditions, and integrating them, versus simple one-dimensional assertion.
right_feature.spec: Read only OC_comments (JSON list of comments by users other than the OP). Parse the list. Rate the cognitive complexity of the counterarguments as one integer 0-10. Cognitive complexity = degree to which the comments differentiate multiple perspectives, factors or conditions, acknowledge nuance/trade-offs/qualifications, and integrate them into a reasoned whole. Anchors: 0 = no reasoning content (e.g., a bare remark); 2 = single simple assertion or one-dimensional claim with no qualification; 5 = some reasoning with a couple of considerations or a qualification, but little integration; 8 = multiple distinct considerations or perspectives, explicit nuance/conditions, partly integrated; 10 = highly differentiated and integrated, weighing several perspectives and conditions into a coherent synthesis. Aggregation assumption (operational, not from the hypothesis): judge the row's comments together as a whole, scoring the most cognitively complex comment's reasoning; do not reward length, number of comments, politeness or emotion per se. Exclude moderator/bot notices. Exclude any OP view-change or delta-award announcements, post-outcome thank-you/resolution updates and any text reporting whether the outcome occurred; generic discussion of delta/platform rules is not an outcome announcement and remains eligible. Use supplied current text; list order is not chronology or rank. Empty list returns null; missing or malformed input returns null. Output a single number 0-10.

right_feature.spec: Read title and argument (OP's view; needed to identify the OP's assumptions) and OC_comments (JSON list of comments by other users, not the OP; parse it). Return 1 if at least one comment explicitly challenges an underlying assumption or premise on which the OP's view rests (e.g. questions a presupposition, definition, value or framing the OP takes for granted), rather than only disputing the OP's factual conclusion or offering a counterexample to the conclusion. Return 0 if no comment does so. A valid empty comment list gives 0. If OC_comments or the OP title/argument is missing or malformed so that this cannot be assessed, return null. Comment order is not meaningful. Ignore and do not use as evidence any OP view-change or delta-award announcements, post-outcome thank-you or resolution updates, or text reporting whether the outcome occurred, including inside argument; generic discussion of delta/platform rules is not an outcome announcement and may be considered. left_feature.spec: Parse OC_comments (JSON list of comments by users other than the OP; list order is not chronology or rank). Use title and argument only as context for identifying the OP. Return 0 if the list is valid and no comment qualifies (including purely logical refutations). Return null if OC_comments is missing or malformed; an empty valid list returns 0. Ignore any OP view-change/delta-award announcements, post-outcome thank-you/resolution updates and text reporting whether the outcome occurred, wherever they appear; generic discussion of delta/platform rules is not an outcome announcement. Output a single 0/1 value or null.

Aggregation assumption (operational, not from the hypothesis): judge the row's comments together as a whole, scoring the most cognitively complex comment's reasoning; do not reward length, number of comments, politeness or emotion per se. Exclude moderator/bot notices. Exclude any OP view-change or delta-award announcements, post-outcome thank-you/resolution updates and any text reporting whether the outcome occurred; generic discussion of delta/platform rules is not an outcome announcement and remains eligible. Use supplied current text; list order is not chronology or rank. Empty list returns null; missing or malformed input returns null. Output a single number 0-10.

right_feature.spec: Read OC_comments (JSON list of comments by users other than the OP; parse it) and the OP's title and argument as context for what counts as OP wording. Return 1 if at least one comment directly quotes wording from the OP's title or argument (verbatim or near-verbatim text reproduced as a quotation, e.g. in quote markup or quotation marks, matching available OP text). The comment need not agree with, endorse or refute the quote. Do not count quotations of other sources, or paraphrases without quoted wording. Return 0 if the list is valid and no comment quotes OP wording, provided title and argument are available; return 0 for a valid empty list. Return null if OC_comments is missing/malformed or if title or argument is missing so absence cannot be established (a clear positive match against available OP text still gives 1). Never use as evidence OP view-change or delta-award announcements, post-outcome thank-you/resolution updates, or any text reporting whether the outcome occurred, even if in the argument; do not treat quotations of such text as qualifying. Generic discussion of platform/delta rules is not an outcome announcement and may be retained. Use current supplied text; do not infer initial snapshots or chronology.

left_feature.name: op_argument_has_counter_question
left_feature.definition: OP argument: contains at least one specific counter-question marker, i.e. an explicit question posed to challenge or counter an opposing view or invite a rebuttal.
left_feature.spec: Read only the OP's argument text (not the title, comments or conversation). Return 1 if the argument contains at least one specific counter-question marker: an explicit question (usually with a question mark or interrogative wording) that the OP poses to challenge, counter, or probe an opposing or possible opposing position, or to invite a rebuttal of the view. Return 0 if the argument is present and has no such question. Rhetorical or genuine questions count only if they function as a counter-question in this sense. Questions that are purely incidental or purely a clarification of the OP's own meaning, and questions inside quoted external text not adopted by the OP, do not count. Exclude and ignore any OP view-change or delta-award announcements, post-outcome thank-you or resolution updates, and any text reporting whether the outcome occurred, even if they contain questions. Generic discussion of delta or platform rules is not an outcome announcement and remains eligible. Use the supplied current text including marked edits; do not try to reconstruct an initial version. Return null if the argument is missing or malformed. Output a single 0/1 value.

right_feature.spec: Read OC_comments (JSON list of comments by users other than the OP; parse it) with title and argument as context to identify the OP's view. Return 1 if at least one comment gives a substantive counterargument: a reasoned or evidence-based challenge to the OP's stated view or its premises. Return 0 if no comment does (e.g., all comments are supportive, agreeing, or merely non-substantive such as jokes, or bare disagreement without reasons). Use current supplied text; do not infer edit timing or chronology; list order carries no meaning. Empty list gives 0; missing/malformed OC_comments gives null.

left_feature.spec: Read title and argument (OP context, to identify the OP's premise) and OC_comments (JSON list of comments by other users, not the OP). Return 1 if at least one comment explicitly acknowledges that the OP's premise/central claim (or a part of it) is valid, correct or reasonable, and then, later in that same comment, introduces a divergence (disagreement, caveat, counterpoint or alternative view). The acknowledgment must come before the divergence within the comment; acknowledgment alone without divergence, divergence without prior explicit validity acknowledgment, or mere politeness/agreement on unrelated points does not qualify. Ignore quoted text from others that the comment does not adopt. Ignore moderator/bot notices. Exclude and never use as evidence any OP view-change or delta-award announcements, post-outcome thank-you/resolution updates, or text reporting whether the outcome occurred, even if in argument; generic discussion of delta/platform rules is not an outcome announcement. Use supplied current text; list order carries no chronology. Return 0 if the comment list is valid and empty or no comment qualifies. Return null if OC_comments is missing/malformed or the OP context needed to identify the premise is missing.

right_feature.name: share_oc_comments_quoting_op
right_feature.definition: Other-user comments: share of comments in the list that directly quote the original post's (title or argument) wording; endorsement or refutation not required.
right_feature.spec: Read OC_comments (JSON list of comments by users other than the OP; parse it) together with the OP's title and argument as context for what counts as OP wording. For each comment decide whether it contains a direct quotation of wording from the OP's title or argument (verbatim or near-verbatim text, typically in quotation marks or block-quote markup, that matches available OP text). Endorsement, refutation or agreement is not required. Paraphrases without quoted wording do not count; quoting other commenters or external sources does not count. Ignore and do not count quotations of OP view-change/delta-award announcements, post-outcome thank-you/resolution updates or any text reporting whether the outcome occurred (even if in argument); generic discussion of delta/platform rules remains eligible text. Use current supplied text; do not infer timing. Output the number of comments with a qualifying quote divided by the total number of comments in the list (range 0 to 1; 0 if none quote). If OC_comments is an empty list return null; if OC_comments, title or argument is missing/malformed such that quote matching cannot be determined return null (a positive match with available OP text may still be returned as such only if the comment share can be computed).

right_feature.spec: Read title, argument (OP's view; context to identify which component of the OP's argument a comment addresses) and OC_comments (JSON list of comments by other users, not the OP). Parse the list. Return 1 if at least one single comment, within that same comment, (a) explicitly acknowledges that a specific identifiable component (claim, premise, or point) of the OP's argument is valid/correct/reasonable, and then (b) afterwards presents a counter-example (a specific case or instance that runs against the OP's view or claim). Both must occur in the same comment and in that order; separate comments cannot jointly satisfy it. Generic politeness, vague agreement, or acknowledgment of the OP as a whole without a specific component does not count; acknowledgment without a subsequent counter-example does not count. Counter-example need not be externally verified. Return 0 if the list is valid and nonempty (or empty) and no comment qualifies; an empty list gives 0. Return null if OC_comments is missing/malformed or if OP context needed to identify the component is missing. Ignore any OP view-change/delta-award announcements, post-outcome thank-you/resolution updates, or any text reporting whether the outcome occurred, even if in argument or comments; do not use them as evidence. Generic discussion of delta/platform rules is not an outcome announcement and may be considered. Use supplied current text; no initial snapshot is inferred. Output 0, 1 or null.

Hypothetical scenarios, general statistics, abstract principles, and quotations of others' experiences not adopted by the commenter do not count. Ignore any text in comments that is an OP view-change/delta-award announcement, post-outcome thank-you/resolution update, or text reporting whether the outcome occurred; generic discussion of delta/platform rules is not an announcement and stays eligible. Return 0 if the list is valid and no comment qualifies, including an empty list. Return null if OC_comments is missing or malformed. Output a single 0/1 per row.

Aggregation assumption (operational, not from the hypothesis): judge the row's comments together as a whole, scoring the most cognitively complex comment's reasoning; do not reward length, number of comments, politeness or emotion per se. Exclude moderator/bot notices. Exclude any OP view-change or delta-award announcements, post-outcome thank-you/resolution updates and any text reporting whether the outcome occurred; generic discussion of delta/platform rules is not an outcome announcement and remains eligible. Use supplied current text; list order is not chronology or rank. Empty list returns null; missing or malformed input returns null. Output a single number 0-10.

left_feature.spec: Read title and argument (OP's view, for target context) and parse OC_comments (JSON list of comments by other users, not the OP). Return 1 if at least one comment directly counterargues the OP's view: it explicitly gives reasons, evidence or logic opposing the OP's main claim or a stated supporting claim. Return 0 if no comment does so (e.g. only questions, agreement, clarifications, jokes, off-topic, or purely tangential remarks). Ignore any OP view-change/delta-award announcements, post-outcome thank-you/resolution updates and any text reporting whether the outcome occurred, even if in the argument; do not use them as evidence. Generic discussion of platform/delta rules is not an outcome announcement and may be considered. Empty valid comment list -> 0. Missing/malformed OC_comments or title/argument unavailable so target cannot be identified -> null. Output a single 0/1 value.

right_feature.name: share_oc_comments_quoting_op
right_feature.definition: Other-user comments: share of comments in the list that directly quote the original post's (title or argument) wording; endorsement or refutation not required.
right_feature.spec: Read OC_comments (JSON list of comments by users other than the OP; parse it) together with the OP's title and argument as context for what counts as OP wording. For each comment decide whether it contains a direct quotation of wording from the OP's title or argument (verbatim or near-verbatim text, typically in quotation marks or block-quote markup, that matches available OP text). Endorsement, refutation or agreement is not required. Paraphrases without quoted wording do not count; quoting other commenters or external sources does not count. Ignore and do not count quotations of OP view-change/delta-award announcements, post-outcome thank-you/resolution updates or any text reporting whether the outcome occurred (even if in argument); generic discussion of delta/platform rules remains eligible text. Use current supplied text; do not infer timing. Output the number of comments with a qualifying quote divided by the total number of comments in the list (range 0 to 1; 0 if none quote). If OC_comments is an empty list return null; if OC_comments, title or argument is missing/malformed such that quote matching cannot be determined return null (a positive match with available OP text may still be returned as such only if the comment share can be computed).

right_feature.spec: Read OC_comments (JSON list of comments by users other than the OP) and, for context on what the OP already said, title and argument. Return 1 if at least one comment explicitly states a verifiable external fact (a specific checkable factual claim, statistic, historical/scientific/legal event, study or cited source; external verification is not performed) that is distinct from, i.e. not merely restating, the facts or claims in the OP's title/argument. Opinions, pure reasoning, hypotheticals, and rephrasings of OP content do not count. Judge each comment separately; one qualifying comment suffices. Return 0 if the list is valid and no comment qualifies. Return 0 for a valid empty list; return null if OC_comments is missing or malformed, or if OP context needed to judge distinctness is missing. Ignore any OP view-change or delta-award announcements, post-outcome thank-you/resolution updates, and any text reporting whether the outcome occurred, even if inside argument or comments; generic discussion of delta/platform rules remains eligible text. Use current supplied text; no initial snapshot is inferred.

left_feature.name: op_hedged_uncertain_epistemic_marker_intensity
left_feature.definition: OP argument: 0-10 score of how strongly the OP's own claims use modest or uncertain epistemic markers (hedges, low-modality wording, explicit uncertainty).
left_feature.spec: Read only the OP's argument text (current supplied text, including marked edits). Ignore any OP view-change/delta-award announcements, post-outcome thank-you or resolution updates, and any text reporting whether the outcome occurred; generic discussion of delta/platform rules is not an outcome announcement and stays eligible. Do not try to reconstruct an initial version. Evaluate only the OP's own assertions; exclude quoted external text or opponents' positions unless the OP adopts them. Score 0-10 for the degree to which the OP's own claims are expressed with modest/uncertain epistemic markers (e.g. may, might, perhaps, I think, to my knowledge, I'm not sure, seems). Anchors: 0 = no such markers; 2 = a few isolated hedges on minor points; 5 = hedging is clearly present on a substantial share of claims, mixed with unhedged claims; 8 = most key claims hedged; 10 = pervasive explicit uncertainty throughout. Aggregation assumption: judge the whole argument holistically, weighting central claims more. Missing or empty argument -> null. Output one number 0-10.

right_feature.name: op_acknowledges_alternative_perspectives

right_feature.spec: Read only the OP's argument text (current text, including marked edits). Return 1 if the OP, in their own voice, explicitly acknowledges the existence of alternative perspectives, other viewpoints, or opposing positions on the issue (e.g., noting that others see it differently or that reasonable people disagree). Return 0 if the argument is assessable and contains no such explicit acknowledgment (presents the view without recognizing alternatives). Do not count opposing positions quoted or reported solely to dismiss them without acknowledging them as existing perspectives only if they are not framed as alternatives; a mere mention of an opponent's view that is explicitly recognized as another perspective counts. Exclude any OP view-change or delta-award announcements, post-outcome thank-you/resolution updates, and any text reporting whether the outcome occurred; ignore them as evidence. Generic discussion of delta/platform rules is not an outcome announcement and may be considered. Do not infer or reconstruct an initial snapshot by removing edits. Return null if argument is missing or malformed. Output 0 or 1.

right_feature.name: counterargument_cognitive_complexity
right_feature.definition: Other-user counterargument comments: overall cognitive complexity (0-10) of the reasoning, i.e. differentiating multiple perspectives/considerations, acknowledging nuance or conditions, and integrating them, versus simple one-dimensional assertion.
right_feature.spec: Read only OC_comments (JSON list of comments by users other than the OP). Parse the list. Rate the cognitive complexity of the counterarguments as one integer 0-10. right_feature.spec: Read OC_comments (JSON list of comments by other users, not the OP), with title and argument only as context for the OP's view. Return 1 if at least one comment opens by directly contradicting or rejecting the OP's view as a whole (blanket contradiction) without first acknowledging any validity in it. Return 0 if no comment does so. Empty list: 0. Missing or malformed OC_comments: null. List order is not chronology or rank. Ignore any OP view-change/delta-award announcements, post-outcome thank-you/resolution updates, and any text reporting whether the outcome occurred, including inside argument; generic discussion of delta/platform rules is not an outcome announcement. Moderator/bot notices do not count. Output 0 or 1.

left_feature.name: op_argument_acknowledges_counterargument_or_limitation
left_feature.definition: OP argument: explicitly acknowledges a counter-argument or a limitation of the OP's own view or argument (1/0).
left_feature.spec: Read only the OP's argument text (current supplied text, including marked edits). Return 1 if the OP, in their own voice, explicitly acknowledges a counter-argument, opposing consideration, or limitation/weakness of their own view or argument (e.g., 'one counterpoint is...', 'I admit this may not hold when...'). Return 0 if the text is assessable and contains no such explicit acknowledgment. Do not count quoted or reported opponents' positions that the OP does not themselves acknowledge, nor mere general uncertainty without naming a counter-argument or limitation. Exclude and do not use as evidence any OP view-change or delta-award announcements, post-outcome thank-you/resolution updates, or text reporting whether the outcome occurred (even within the argument); generic discussion of delta/platform rules is not an outcome announcement and may be considered if relevant. Return null if argument is missing or malformed. Output a single 0/1.

right_feature.spec: Read OC_comments (JSON list of comments by users other than the OP) jointly with the OP title and argument as context. Return 1 if at least one comment explicitly quotes (quote markup or verbatim OP wording) or explicitly references a specific identifiable textual element of the OP's title or argument (a particular sentence, phrase, claim or example the OP wrote), whether or not it agrees with, endorses or refutes it. Merely discussing the OP's general topic does not count. Quotes of text not from the OP do not count. Exclude from OP context any OP view-change/delta-award announcements, post-outcome thank-you/resolution updates, and any text reporting whether the outcome occurred; do not use such text to establish a match. Generic discussion of delta/platform rules is allowed. Use current supplied text; do not infer an initial snapshot or chronology from list order. Return 0 if the comment list is validly empty or no comment qualifies given available OP text. Return null if OC_comments is missing or malformed, or if both OP title and argument are missing so absence cannot be determined (an observed match to available OP text may still be 1).

right_feature.spec: Read OC_comments (JSON list of comments by users other than the OP) jointly with the OP title and argument as context. Return 1 if at least one comment explicitly quotes (quote markup or verbatim OP wording) or explicitly references a specific identifiable textual element of the OP's title or argument (a particular sentence, phrase, claim or example the OP wrote), whether or not it agrees with, endorses or refutes it. Merely discussing the OP's general topic does not count. Quotes of text not from the OP do not count. Exclude from OP context any OP view-change/delta-award announcements, post-outcome thank-you/resolution updates, and any text reporting whether the outcome occurred; do not use such text to establish a match. Generic discussion of delta/platform rules is allowed. Use current supplied text; do not infer an initial snapshot or chronology from list order. Return 0 if the comment list is validly empty or no comment qualifies given available OP text. Return null if OC_comments is missing or malformed, or if both OP title and argument are missing so absence cannot be determined (an observed match to available OP text may still be 1).

Exclude any OP view-change/delta-award announcement, post-outcome thank-you/resolution update or outcome-reporting text in the title (not generic discussion of delta/platform rules); such text is not evidence. Return null if the title is missing or malformed. Output a single 0/1 value.

left_feature.spec: Read only the OP's argument text (current supplied text, including marked edits). Exclude OP view-change/delta-award announcements, post-outcome thank-you/resolution updates and any text reporting whether the outcome occurred; generic discussion of delta/platform rules is not an outcome announcement and stays eligible. Exclude quoted text attributed to others unless the OP adopts it. Score the OP's own claims about their view on 0-10: 0 = no hedging at all, claims entirely absolute/unqualified declaratives (e.g., always/never/obviously, no qualifiers); 2-3 = occasional isolated qualifiers amid mostly absolute claims; 5 = mixed, roughly balanced hedged and absolute claims; 7-8 = most central claims hedged or qualified (e.g., may, might, I think, probably, in most cases, to my knowledge); 10 = virtually all claims tentative or heavily qualified. Assumption: the row score reflects the overall balance and prominence of hedging across the argument, weighted toward the central claims. Hedging density is not a frequency cutoff; no threshold is applied. If argument is missing or empty, return null.

right_feature.spec: Read OC_comments (JSON list of other users' comments; parse it). For each comment decide whether it contains at least one explicit agreement marker in the commenter's own voice: an overt statement expressing agreement or concurrence (e.g. 'I agree', 'you're right', 'fair point', 'exactly', 'I concede that part'). Agreement may be with the OP or partial, and the list of examples is nonexhaustive. Do not count agreement attributed to others, quoted opposing positions, or moderator/bot notices; do not count implicit alignment without explicit wording. Return the number of comments with such a marker divided by the total number of comments (range 0 to 1; 0 means no comment contains one). Empty valid list or missing/malformed OC_comments gives null. Exclude and never use as evidence any OP view-change or delta-award announcements, post-outcome thank-you/resolution updates, or text reporting whether the outcome occurred; generic discussion of delta/platform rules is not an outcome announcement. Use supplied current text only; do not infer chronology. Output one number or null.

Return 0 if the title has no such explicit absolute term. Do not count terms that are only implied, and do not count the 'CMV:' prefix. Variable/probabilistic terms do not count here. Ignore any OP view-change/delta-award announcements, post-outcome thank-you/resolution text or outcome-reporting text if present (generic discussion of delta rules is not an outcome announcement). Return null if title is missing or malformed.

Generic discussion of delta/platform rules is not an outcome announcement and may be considered. Use supplied current text; no initial snapshot is inferred. Output 0, 1 or null.
